evidence.experimental_conditions: 48 h exposure; murine bone marrow-derived dendritic cells; flow cytometry
evidence.support_text: Murine bone marrow-derived dendritic cells (BMDCs) were exposed to the allergen nickel sulfate (NiSO4) for 48 h. Surface expression of MHC class II, CD40, CD54, and CD86 was measured by flow cytometry. NiSO4, as one of six allergens tested, induced a significant increase in marker expression, with the percentage of mature cells increased 2.3- to 10.5-fold over control.

evidence.experimental_conditions: in vitro generated human dendritic cells from blood, Ni-NTA enrichment, 2-D electrophoresis, mass spectrometry
evidence.support_text: Using in vitro generated human dendritic cells (DCs) and a Ni-NTA enrichment proteomics approach, the authors identified 32 Ni-interacting proteins out of 57 isolated proteins, demonstrating that nickel binds to multiple proteins in DCs.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Peripheral blood mononuclear cells from 13 nickel-sensitive subjects cultured with nickel sulphate for 7 days
evidence.support_text: Nickel sulphate induced blast transformation reactions were performed with peripheral blood mononuclear cells of 13 nickel sensitive subjects. Most of the induced blasts bear αβ T cell receptors (57±11%) and a few bear γδ receptors (5±5%). The blasts are predominantly helper cells (CD4) and bear memory cell marker (CD45RO), IL-2 receptors and HLA-DR.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Human Raji B cells
evidence.support_text: Nickel (Ni) bound to 28 proteins in human Raji B cells, including heat shock proteins, chaperones, and cytoskeletal proteins; direct binding was demonstrated for the TRiC/CCT complex and HSP70.
